text:
emma: just saw a support ticket where Next middleware on Vercel throws "ReferenceError: process is not defined" when importing our SDK. stack shows it landed in a tiny util shim we didn't expect in edge builds.

josh: hmm — likely pulled a node-only helper from our esm build. edge runtime doesn't have process, globalThis.fetch is present though. are folks importing the top-level package?

emma: yes, they did `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` in middleware.ts. their bundler pulled the CJS entry because package.json lacks a clear ESM/edge map.

priya: two problems colliding: 1) conditional exports not pointing to an edge-optimized entry so bundlers choose the wrong file, 2) types resolution points at the CJS dts which confuses TS in editors.

marco: concrete fix proposal: add a dedicated subpath `@redwood/inference/edge` and an `exports` map entry like "./edge": { "import": "./dist/edge/index.mjs", "types": "./dist/edge/index.d.ts" }. keep the main exports for node server usage.

emma: +1. also keep the edge file minimal — re-export the runtime surface only, don't import any node shims or polyfills. add `export default` to that entry so plain JS consumers don't get tripped by named vs default export.

josh: for builds: produce a third build target `dist/edge` via esbuild with `platform: browser`, `target: es2020`, and `external: ['fs','child_process','crypto']` to ensure no node internals leak in.

priya: typings: generate d.ts for the edge entry and reference it in the exports map. VSCode/tsserver will then resolve `@redwood/inference/edge` correctly. avoid pointing top-level `types` to CJS-only dts.

marco: CI additions: 1) smoke test that installs the published package into a small Next fixture and runs `next build` 2) run `tsc --noEmit` in the fixture 3) an esbuild bundle check: `esbuild --bundle example/entry.ts --platform=browser --target=es2020` and assert output doesn't contain `process` or `require(`.

emma: docs: add explicit onboarding note: "When using the SDK from edge runtimes (Vercel Edge, Next middleware), import from `@redwood/inference/edge` and ensure your bundler targets es2020+ and doesn't polyfill node globals." include the tiny middleware snippet and a one-line troubleshooting checklist.

josh: will add a tiny factory shim for the edge entry to keep ergonomics: `import { Redwood } from '../esm/index.mjs'; export default Redwood; export { Redwood };`. that avoids copying code and keeps runtime surface identical.

priya: one last gotcha: some bundlers (older SWC/esbuild) may still inject AbortController shims with different shapes. we'll document tests: confirm `new Request()` behaves as expected in a Vercel-like environment.

docs-bot: PR #1583 opened: add edge subpath, edge build, types, and CI smoke tests. Preview docs updated at /docs/edge-sdk.

emma: assigning follow-ups: josh (edge build + default export shim), priya (d.ts and package.json exports), marco (CI fixture), me (docs + support KB). will review PR today. thanks all :rocket:
